notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 15 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingengineer1515cont), the 26 weekly issues from 6 January to 30 June 1915, the first volume of the run. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1914-1917, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1915. The labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. The OCR garbles many item numbers, so extract.py was run with BEN_LOOSE=1, which also takes an entry under a type heading whose number it cannot read; the item numbers of the published rows were then read from the page image, and unresolved rows whose number was not read carry no extra.item and say so in the locator. Every published row was read against the page image, location first, ; a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out (the total of the marble contract at 753 Bush Street is cut off at the column edge, and one dwelling at 28th Avenue north of Ulloa has no legible cost); costs that run into the next column or leaf were read there. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's own address or beside the building site that name is cut too, with the owner firm. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices (printed in this volume as dated lines without item numbers), liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the mastheads (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, four leaves before the masthead that prints 'San Francisco' and the date). The raw text of the published rows is the OCR text corrected against the image, with the names and cost the image shows. Four single houses that were read against the image and have no architect or no name left to publish sit with the held single houses. Five held facts whose parcels got a page from this volume were read against their page images and published: 1918 basement and garage work at 192 20th Avenue, 1921 fire repairs at 305 Spruce Street, a 1924 bake oven at 500 Haight Street, a 1926 sun porch at 85 Palm Avenue and 1931 restaurant alterations at 2263 Chestnut Street.

coverage.remaining: All 34 half-year volumes are read (January 1915 to January 1932). In this volume: 186 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but four still need the image check). 471 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 660 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 2,491 numbered entries read, 1,556 San Francisco rows, 896 placed on a parcel, 243 picked and read against the page image, 191 published on 181 pages (80 seeded), 48 held back: 38 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, six pieces of minor work, two contracts printed in the same issue as their permits and two alterations located only by a distance along the street with nothing to confirm the street number; four more joined the held houses.
